name: PAD Amputation Re-amputation and Mortality — Synthetic Data Module (pad_amp v2)
remarks: PURPOSE
Adds amputation PROGRESSION signal to the pad_amp dataset for pad-bka-aka-prog,
the external validation of AMPREDICT MoRe (Norvell et al., Eur J Vasc Endovasc
pad_amp v1 has ZERO re-amputation signal — all 198 index-amputation patients
have exactly one amputation date — and 1 year mortality of only 4.0%.
DESIGN: DISCRETE-TIME COMPETING RISKS, 12 MONTHLY SLICES
REVISED 2026-08-06. An earlier draft sampled MoRe's four-category outcome up
front and then emitted events to match it. That was wrong, for three reasons:
1. COMPETING RISKS DISAPPEARED. A pre-assigned death-no-re-amputation
patient was never AT RISK of re-amputation. In reality they were at risk
and died first. So the data could not exercise censoring — and censoring
is exactly what a cohort SQL gets wrong.
2. THE TEMPORAL LOGIC BECAME UNTESTABLE. The whole point of this dataset is
to test the 1-365 vs 22-365 day window distinction. Fixing the ANSWER at
time zero made the windows decoration.
3. IT WAS MORE COMPLEX, NOT LESS. In Synthea, module processing STOPS when a
patient dies, so competing risks are free if events are allowed to play
out. The earlier draft built routing to simulate what the engine does.
So the four categories are now EMERGENT — a derived label checked in QC, not
an input. Each patient walks 12 monthly slices; in each slice a re-amputation
hazard fires, then a death hazard. Death ends the timeline on its own.
HAZARDS — SOLVED, not guessed. And they encode real DEPENDENCE.
Solved 2026-08-06 against all four published cells simultaneously.
⭐ THE INTERESTING FINDING: MoRe's published four-category split is NOT
consistent with INDEPENDENT hazards. Hazards tuned to hit both marginals
exactly (re-amputation 28.0%, death 19.4%) produce D/R = 3.3%, but MoRe
reports 5.1%. Re-amputation and death are therefore POSITIVELY DEPENDENT in
the real data — which is clinically expected: a re-amputation is both a marker
of severity and a surgical insult.
Encoding that dependence as an elevated post-re-amputation death hazard fits
all four cells to within 0.09 percentage points TOTAL:
monthly re-amputation hazard, TT (base) : 0.0288
monthly death hazard, no re-amputation  : 0.0156
monthly death hazard, after re-amputation: 0.0289  (= 1.85x baseline)
EMERGENT                published
marginals: re-amp 28.0% (28.0), death 19.4% (19.4)
⚠️ TWO CAVEATS ON THOSE NUMBERS.
* The LEVEL MULTIPLIERS (TM 1.40x, TT 1.00x, TF 0.60x) are a CLINICAL PRIOR,
NOT published. MoRe does not report re-amputation by level. The direction
is defensible — TM has the most room to progress and TF has nowhere higher
to go within MoRe's levels — but the magnitudes are RESEARCHER_ADJUSTS.
They are weighted by the published level mix (33.8/43.7/22.5) so the
overall marginal holds whatever they are set to, but changing them shifts
re-amputation BETWEEN levels.
* The 1.85x dependence multiplier is INFERRED from the published joint
distribution, not stated by MoRe. It is the value that reproduces D/R.
COMPOSED-SYSTEM RESULT (300,000 patients, this module walked end to end with
pad_amp_index_sequence.json, 2026-08-06): ND/NR 57.75 · ND/R 22.72 ·
D/NR 14.43 · D/R 5.10, total error 0.37 pp; marginals 27.81% / 19.53%; level
mix TM 33.69 / TT 43.79 / TF 22.52. The index sequence needs NO hazard
re-solve — its branch (b) additions and branch (a) day-22 suppression nearly
cancel. ⚠️ ALWAYS re-simulate the COMPOSED system after a retune, never this
module alone: reasoning about the interaction in one direction got it wrong.
A finite real generation (~200 index patients) will still scatter around
these expectations — calibrate in Step 6 QC.
THE POINT: MAKE A WRONG COHORT SQL FAIL
MoRe's level and re-amputation logic CANNOT be expressed in circe — it
classifies on TIMING and ANTECEDENT, not set membership (pad-bka-aka-prog
docs/MODEL_RECREATION.md §14 entry 17). That study must hand-author its cohort
SQL, and hand-authored cohort SQL is the riskiest code in it.
So this module emits NEGATIVE CONTROLS alongside signal — events a naive
implementation will wrongly count. Each sets its own attribute so the
pre-flight can assert an exact expected count rather than eyeball a total.
If the pre-flight passes whether the SQL is right or wrong, the dataset failed.
(amp_decoy_early_revision has MOVED to the base module — see below.)
amp_decoy_contralateral   correct timing, correct level, WRONG LIMB.
amp_decoy_toe_or_ray      never an incident level and never 'same or higher'
than TM/TT/TF. Matters because the workspace's
minor_amputation set CONTAINS toe and ray, so SQL
built from that broad set rather than
forefoot_midfoot_amputation will over-count.
MoRe's RE-AMPUTATION DEFINITION, verbatim (Methods, 'Outcomes')
'Re-amputation was identified by an amputation procedure code that occurred
1 - 365 days after the definitive incident amputation (or 22 - 365 days after
guillotine or disarticulation procedures to allow for revisions within three
weeks) and was ipsilateral to the incident procedure, had unknown laterality,
or was bilateral at the same or higher level than the incident amputation.'
1. TWO windows, not one — selected by amp_index_definitive.
2. UNKNOWN laterality COUNTS, and so does BILATERAL. Only confirmed
contralateral is excluded, so requiring ipsilateral UNDER-counts.
3. SAME OR HIGHER level only.
4. 'It is understood that re-amputation and death could only be counted if
the re-amputation preceded death.' Now guaranteed by CONSTRUCTION: within
a monthly slice the re-amputation check runs BEFORE the death check, and a
dead patient never re-enters the loop.
THREE SUB-TYPES, all counted:
a. soft tissue revision       — TT and TF only
b. re-amputation, same level  — TT and TF; for TM, ANY subsequent TM code
c. definitive at higher level — TM->TT, TM->TF, TT->TF
TM SPECIAL CASE, verbatim: 'Because TM amputations do not have codes for soft
tissue revision or re-amputation at the same level, all TM codes after an
incident TM amputation were coded as a subsequent TM amputation and
classified as a re-amputation at the same level.' Note 'all TM codes' —
BROADER than the ICD-9 84.3 route in §14 entry 18.
⛔ BASE-MODULE CONTRACT: THE GUILLOTINE SEQUENCE IS NOT IN THIS MODULE
MOVED OUT 2026-08-06. An earlier version of this module emitted the guillotine
closure itself. That was wrong twice over:
1. WRONG CODE. It emitted SNOMED 180048002 'Revision coverage of amputation
stump' (OMOP 4078404). A guillotine closure is NOT a stump revision — it is
a SECOND DEFINITIVE AMPUTATION CODE AT THE SAME LEVEL. In claims the
sequence is a BKA code and then another BKA code 1-2 weeks later (CPT 27882
open/circular, then definitive 27880; in SNOMED, 88312006 twice).
This also gutted the test: a stump-revision concept is an EASY decoy that a
naive SQL may not even carry in its amputation set. Two IDENTICAL amputation
codes separated only by timing is the dangerous case, and the one worth
building.
2. WRONG PLACE. Per MoRe's Methods, the forward three-week search exists 'to
classify the incident level' — so the closure DEFINES the index event rather
than following it. A guillotine TT closed at TT is an incident TT; closed at
TF, the incident level IS TF. That is index construction, which belongs to
whichever module owns the index procedure. This module declares
amp_index_level and amp_index_definitive as INPUTS — emitting the closure
here contradicted its own interface.
WHAT THE BASE MODULE MUST DO (all three branches — registry acceptance
criterion 2 requires them, and the old version implemented only the first):
a. CLOSURE WITHIN 3 WEEKS (days 1-21). Emit a second DEFINITIVE amputation
code. That code sets amp_index_level:
~85-90%  same level as the guillotine   (TT -> TT, TF -> TF)
~10-15%  escalated at closure           (TT -> TF)
Set amp_index_definitive = false, since MoRe's 22-365 day re-amputation
window applies to these patients. Set amp_decoy_early_revision = true: the
second code is part of the INDEX EVENT and must NOT count as a
re-amputation. This is the strongest negative control in the dataset.
⚠️ Because escalation shifts the level mix toward TF, the base module's
INITIAL level draw must be corrected so the FINAL mix still lands on the
b. CLOSURE AFTER 3 WEEKS (day 22+). MoRe: 'an error in the initial coding was
presumed and the guillotine code was recoded as a definitive amputation.'
So amp_index_level = the GUILLOTINE's level, amp_index_definitive = true,
and the late closure is then ELIGIBLE as a re-amputation. Note this inverts
branch (a): the same code at day 20 vs day 25 flips from index-event to
outcome. That pair is the sharpest test of the two-window rule.
c. NO CLOSURE AT ALL. Same recoding as (b) — amp_index_definitive = true at the
guillotine's level. MoRe states both branches; ref 10 states only the
>3-week one, so an implementation matching ref 10 misses this.
This module then handles ONLY the outcome side, and keeps the day-22 suppression
(Reamp_Window_Eligibility) because that is outcome logic, not index logic.
TWO OPEN PROBLEMS. READ BEFORE GENERATING.
1. TODO [VOCAB] GUILLOTINE HAS NO SNOMED CONCEPT. Verified against local
omop_vocab 2026-08-06: the only guillotine-amputation concepts are CPT4 —
27882 (OMOP 2105448) and 27592 (OMOP 2105211), both standard. Every SNOMED
'guillotine' hit is unrelated (tonsillectomy, paper cutter, execution).
The guillotine INDEX event belongs to the base module, but this module's
day-22 window depends on it. If the ETL cannot carry CPT4 — the existing
pad_amp_dispo module emits only SNOMED-CT/RxNorm/LOINC — the 22-365 window
is untestable and registry acceptance criterion 2 cannot be met.
Do NOT quietly substitute a definitive code: that hides the gap behind a
passing pre-flight.
2. TODO [ETL] LATERALITY IS NOT EMITTED. Synthea has no procedure-laterality
field, so the ipsilateral / unknown / bilateral arms and the contralateral
decoy are INDISTINGUISHABLE downstream until the ETL populates
procedure_occurrence.modifier_source_value or an ICD-10-PCS body-part
character. Until then the contralateral decoy will read as a false positive
that looks like a SQL bug. Resolve before scoring that control.
REQUIRED INPUT ATTRIBUTES (set by the base/index module)
amp_index_level      'TM' | 'TT' | 'TF'  incident level (mix 33.8/43.7/22.5)
amp_index_definitive true | false        false = guillotine/disarticulation
index, selecting the 22-365 window
OUTPUT ATTRIBUTES, for the QC queries:
amp_month, amp_reamp_occurred, amp_reamp_subtype, amp_reamp_laterality,
amp_death_1y, amp_decoy_early_revision, amp_decoy_contralateral,
amp_decoy_toe_or_ray
TODO [COMPOSE] Module composition is not wired (Step 3 hard-fails on extra
workspace-authored modules; Step 4 runs Synthea with no -m filter), so merge
these states into pad_amp_dispo.json as a sub-graph for now. EXACTLY ONE
module may own the index procedure — two owners caused the v1 379->196
inflation.
Only patients with an incident amputation enter. Fails CLOSED: if the base
module did not set amp_index_level, nothing fires and no spurious
progression is emitted.
Explicit false rather than nil, so the QC query can distinguish 'checked, did not happen' from 'never evaluated'.
Slice 1..12. The loop exit tests amp_month >= 12.
One monthly slice. 30-31 days, so 12 slices span ~360-372 days rather than
exactly 365. That JITTER IS DELIBERATE: it puts some events either side of
the day-365 boundary, which is precisely where an off-by-one in the cohort
SQL shows up. A fixed 30 days would total 360 and never test the boundary.
⚠️ Consequence for QC: a small number of month-12 events land after day 365
and must NOT be counted. The QC query has to assert that, not assume it.
MoRe's outcome is BINARY 'any re-amputation', so once a patient has one
there is nothing more to detect and further re-amputation checks are
skipped. Death hazard continues — at the ELEVATED rate.
Per-level monthly hazard. Level multipliers are a CLINICAL PRIOR, not
published — see the header. Weighted by the published level mix so the
overall 28.0% marginal holds regardless of how they are tuned.
TM: 0.0403/month (1.40x base). Most room to progress. RESEARCHER_ADJUSTS.
TT: 0.0288/month — the solved base rate.
TF: 0.0173/month (0.60x base). No higher LE level exists within MoRe's scheme. RESEARCHER_ADJUSTS.
THE TWO-WINDOW RULE, applied where it actually bites. In month 1 a
GUILLOTINE/disarticulation index is still inside MoRe's day 1-21 exclusion,
so a hazard draw here is SUPPRESSED — not eligible yet, and no event is
emitted. From month 2 onward (day >= 30) both windows are open.
A definitive index has no exclusion, so month 1 counts normally.
This is the state that makes a single-window implementation detectable.
Sub-type availability depends on the INCIDENT level — the crux of MoRe's
algorithm. TM has NO soft-tissue-revision or same-level codes, so any
subsequent TM code IS the same-level re-amputation. TF has no higher level.
A single sub-type router for all levels would emit TT-only codes for TM
patients and silently make the TM stratum unvalidatable.
RESEARCHER_ADJUSTS. Both arms must stay non-trivial or the 'all TM codes count' rule is never exercised.
All three sub-types available. RESEARCHER_ADJUSTS.
No higher LE level above TF in MoRe's scheme, so revision and same-level only. This asymmetry is real.
Sub-type (a). SNOMED-CT 180048002 -> OMOP 4078404 [vocab query 2026-08-06,
standard, Procedure]. Also the 'Maps to' target of ICD-9 84.3, the revision
code MoRe's ref 11 used. TT/TF only — TM bypasses this state.

remarks: The canonical progression MoRe cites (TT -> TF).
Ground truth for QC: compare against what the cohort SQL detects, per sub-type and per level.
MoRe counts IPSILATERAL, UNKNOWN, or BILATERAL. Only confirmed
contralateral is excluded, so an implementation requiring ipsilateral
UNDER-counts — hence the unknown and bilateral arms exist to catch that.
⚠️ TODO [ETL]: Synthea emits no laterality, so these arms are documentation
of intent until the ETL populates a modifier. RESEARCHER_ADJUSTS.
Monthly death hazard for patients with NO re-amputation yet: 0.0156.
Runs AFTER the re-amputation check in the same slice, which is what makes
MoRe's 'the re-amputation preceded death' constraint structural.
ELEVATED monthly death hazard after a re-amputation: 0.0289 = 1.85x the
0.0156 baseline. This multiplier is what reproduces MoRe's D/R cell (5.1%);
independent hazards give only 3.3%. INFERRED from the published joint
distribution, not stated by MoRe — see the header.
Sets death_date, which the ETL writes to the OMOP death table. Synthea
STOPS module processing here — which is precisely why competing risks now
work for free: a patient who dies never re-enters the monthly loop and so
is correctly no longer at risk of re-amputation.
NEGATIVE CONTROLS, emitted as a small monthly hazard so they spread across
the year like real events, while each still sets an attribute so QC can
assert an exact expected count. ~1.5%/month gives roughly 1 in 6 patients
at least one decoy over 12 months. RESEARCHER_ADJUSTS.
DECOY 2 — correct timing, correct level, WRONG LIMB. MoRe excludes only
confirmed contralateral events.
⚠️ TODO [ETL]: without emitted laterality this is indistinguishable from a
real ipsilateral re-amputation and will read as a false positive that looks
like a SQL bug. Resolve before scoring this control.

remarks: DECOY 3 — toe or ray amputation. Neither is an incident level for MoRe
(TM/TT/TF only) and neither is 'same or higher' than any of them.
This control exists because the workspace's minor_amputation set CONTAINS
toe and ray, so SQL built from that broad set rather than
forefoot_midfoot_amputation ([DVI] 1891165) will wrongly count these.
See catalog toe_amputation ([DVI] 1891164).
SNOMED-CT 371186005 -> OMOP 4159766 [vocab query 2026-08-06]. In toe_amputation, NOT in forefoot_midfoot_amputation.
SNOMED-CT 405443002 -> OMOP 4226945 [vocab query 2026-08-06]. A ray removes
ONE metatarsal with its toe, so it is NOT transmetatarsal (which requires
removal of ALL toes) — verified 2026-08-06 that 4226945 is a SIBLING of both
the toe and TMA anchors, not a descendant of either.
